terms.definition: The length of time a pollutant remains in the environment before it breaks down.
terms.examiner: Persistent pollutants travel further and can build up.

terms.definition: The build-up of a substance in the tissues of an organism over its lifetime.
terms.examiner: Happens with substances that are liposoluble and persistent.

terms.definition: The increase in concentration of a substance at each higher trophic level of a food chain.
terms.examiner: Top predators are affected most; do not confuse it with bioaccumulation in one organism.

terms.definition: When two pollutants together have a greater effect than the sum of their separate effects.
terms.examiner: Ozone and sulfur dioxide on plants is an example.

terms.definition: The ability of a substance to dissolve in fats and oils.
terms.examiner: Liposoluble substances cross cell membranes and are stored in fatty tissue.

terms.definition: A layer of warm air above cooler air near the ground, which traps pollutants.
terms.examiner: Common in valleys on calm, clear nights; explains smog episodes.

terms.definition: Predicting the routes a pollutant will take through the environment to find where it will become most concentrated.
terms.examiner: Used to decide where to monitor, for example for radioactive discharges.

terms.definition: A substance that causes changes to DNA.
terms.examiner: A carcinogen causes cancer; a teratogen causes birth abnormalities.
